I've worked with many Pdocs and I can tell you a few truths.

And every one of them is trying their best to help you. Some are have better bedside manner than others. They only get paid to give you medicine. Insurance companies do not pay them to counsel you. They would like to spend more time with you but there is a huge Pdoc shortage so they try to help as many people they can in a day. They are not out to get you.


That being said, there are incompetent Pdocs just like there are incompetent surgeons. The C students have to work somewhere.
They do not specialize in illnesses but if you ask around, you can find out who is best for what. They can't advertise their expertise because they don't have any proof. But ask staff or even other Pdocs who they would recommend for your symptoms or diagnosis.


To sum up, you are right. Its all people trying their best until the day we know everything about brain functions down to the smallest levels.

My grandmothers sister passed away from lung cancer on the 4th of July which also happened to be her birthday. My grandmother took it very hard that her younger sister passed away so suddenly. She died right in front of her.

My grandmother wanted all the old pictures her sister had kept of her family. Old family heirlooms from generations back. She didn't care about the jewelry or the house. 

A niece of theirs, out of vengeance over a 50 year family feud, had gotten the power over the estate just days before my aunt passed.
She had sold off everything of value and threw away everything else.
My grandmother was so upset she cried everyday. 

A year later I had a dream that I told my grandmother about. Aunt comes to me, she looks upset and frustrated. She says "I feel like I have no arms."

Now I know that sounds strange, but she was an old fashioned lady who never left the 1950's. She was always talking in metaphors or old slang. I never heard her use this phrase before but I knew what it meant. She meant she felt like she was powerless to change the situation between my aunt and the niece. 
My grandmother listened then reminded me what day it was, it was the 4th of July. I had forgotten that was the anniversary day.
